findings.evidence: Lines 58–66 constrain `toFun` only through `IsPiecewiseC1On toFun a b` and endpoint equality; `IsPiecewiseC1On` itself constrains only `uIcc a b`, while `@[ext]` at line 55 requires equality of the entire `ℝ → ℂ` field.
findings.fix: Store only the interval-restricted curve (with a canonical derived raw-function accessor), or quotient raw bundles by equality of `a`, `b`, and values on `uIcc a b`, then prove the cycle operations descend.
findings.issue: `PiecewiseC1ClosedCurve.toFun : ℝ → ℂ` records values outside `uIcc a b`, although its laws, trace, integral, and winding number only use the parametrized interval; consequently extensionally identical curves can be distinct free generators and cannot cancel.

summary: The cycle generators carry unconstrained function data outside their parameter intervals, so the public cycle type is not extensional on the curves it denotes.
